claim: A one-line code fence that wraps onto multiple PDF baselines fails the release check.
where: README Checks; landing Missing or wrapped code
sandbox: Generated one-page PDF splits one source line across two baselines; assert exit 1, code.flow-changed, and HOLD proof.

claim: Two code fence lines merged into one PDF line fail the release check.
sandbox: Generated PDF paints two source lines as one line; assert exit 1, code.flow-changed, and a failed HTML proof sheet.

claim: Text is checked against every visible PDF page edge.
sandbox: Generated PDFs place text beyond all four MediaBox edges and a non-default CropBox; every case exits 1.

claim: Missing code fence text is reported as a release defect.
sandbox: Generated PDF omits a code fence line; assert exit 1 and code.content-missing.

claim: A Markdown fragment cannot pass with a wrong PDF destination.
sandbox: Generated PDF maps a source fragment to an unrelated destination; assert exit 1 and link.destination-missing.

claim: Missing syntax color warns by default and fails when warnings are denied; unrelated colored headings and graphics do not count.
sandbox: A blue graphic and blue heading precede matching black code; assert its own text still warns, then fails with --deny-warnings.

claim: Page bounds use PDF font widths and text transforms.
sandbox: Embedded wide and narrow glyph widths plus a scaled text matrix produce the correct pass/fail boundaries.

claim: Built-in width tables cover Helvetica and Courier.
sandbox: Generated Helvetica and Courier PDFs place wide and narrow text near the right edge; assert exact pass and overflow boundaries.

claim: Code Proof recognizes # headings, underlined Markdown headings, and Pandoc explicit heading IDs.
sandbox: Each heading form links to a generated retry-policy PDF annotation and named destination; assert full inspection passes.

claim: Link target matching ignores letter case.
sandbox: Mixed-case Markdown heading, link, PDF annotation, and named destination resolve to the same target.

claim: Automatic heading IDs ignore formatting, keep letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens, and periods, replace spaces, lowercase letters, and drop characters before the first letter.
sandbox: Five generated Markdown/PDF pairs assert formatted, retained-character, spaced, mixed-case, leading-number, and leading-punctuation identifiers exactly.

claim: An existing PDF can be checked without starting a renderer.
where: README Usage; landing workflow and safety
sandbox: Fresh temporary Markdown/PDF pair is checked with --pdf; assert PASS JSON and an HTML proof sheet.

claim: The CLI reads the supplied paths and writes HTML proof sheet artifacts locally.
sandbox: Fresh temporary source/PDF paths are supplied to --pdf; assert the requested local proof/index.html is written.

claim: Code Proof does not edit the supplied Markdown source.
sandbox: A fresh Markdown fixture is checked through existing-PDF and custom-renderer paths; compare its bytes after each completed check.

claim: Custom renderer placeholders become individual arguments, never shell input.
sandbox: A temporary renderer receives substituted input/output arguments and produces a checked HTML proof sheet.

claim: Linux renderer subprocesses cannot create network connections.
where: README Renderer safety; landing Renderer safety
sandbox: A sandboxed curl renderer targets a loopback listener; assert that listener receives no connection.

claim: A renderer does not start when Linux sandbox setup fails.
where: README Renderer safety; landing Renderer safety
sandbox: Inject sandbox setup refusal before spawn; assert exit 2 and that a renderer marker file is absent.

claim: A renderer has a deadline set by --timeout.
where: README Renderer safety; landing Renderer safety
sandbox: Run a two-second renderer with --timeout 1; assert exit 2 and deadline diagnostic.

claim: A successful check writes an HTML proof sheet.
sandbox: A valid temporary source/PDF pair exits 0 and writes proof/index.html containing PASS.

claim: A check can write a JSON report for CI.
sandbox: A valid temporary source/PDF pair runs with --json; assert JSON passed:true output.

claim: Exit 0 means pass, exit 1 means defects, and exit 2 means the check could not finish.
sandbox: Valid, defect, and missing-source fixtures assert 0, 1, and 2 respectively.

claim: The bundled sample runs without user files or a renderer and writes a HOLD — do not release HTML proof sheet.
sandbox: Run codeproof demo into a fresh temporary directory; assert bundled sample, generated PDF, code.flow-changed, and HOLD — do not release HTML proof sheet.

claim: The browser demo shows the normalized output of the real bundled CLI demo.
sandbox: Run the built CLI with bundled sample data in a fresh temporary directory, normalize only its path, and compare every displayed output line.

claim: The documentation demo makes only same-origin requests and stores no tracking data.
sandbox: Fresh browser context records request origins, cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage through the demo flow.

claim: The installed documentation shell works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: Dedicated browser context waits for the active service worker, goes offline, reloads, and asserts docs plus offline status.

claim: The deployed site sends its security headers and a branded 404 response.
sandbox: Request the built root and an unknown path; assert CSP, nosniff, referrer policy, permissions policy, HTTP 404, and branded fallback content.

claim: The package and locked dependencies compile with Rust 1.88.
sandbox: Read locked dependency metadata then run cargo +1.88 check --workspace --locked.

claim: The published install command works from an empty directory.
sandbox: Cargo installs codeproof from the public Git repository into a fresh temporary root, then runs --version.

claim: Code Proof is free software under the MIT License.
sandbox: Assert the free-of-charge MIT grant in LICENSE, MIT crate metadata, and matching free-software and license references in the landing page and Terms.
